title: OptiGen AI Platform
summary: A B2B AI platform for managing organizations, permissions, AI bots, and documents while providing RAG-grounded conversations. I designed and implemented the frontend and UI/UX from the ground up, then extended it into business execution and voice channels through MCP and Voice Gateway.

keyOutcome.label: Key Outcome
keyOutcome.value: AI platform foundation extended across POC, DEV, and SOLUM environments
keyOutcome.description: I established the frontend structure and shared UI standards first, so the same development approach could continue as environments and capabilities grew.

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description:
I built the frontend structure and screens from scratch, covering organization, permission, bot, prompt, and document management through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) conversations grounded in documents. I connected bot selection, message composition, response reading, and conversation history in one flow. Navigation, conversation lists, messages, and input tools rearrange to fit the screen size.

I created shared design tokens and components and defined state management responsibilities across React Query, Zustand, and SSE. Forty Storybook stories and a Vitest and Playwright testing setup gave later contributors a shared baseline for extending the product. I used semantic elements and accessible names, then checked keyboard interaction and focus restoration after closing modals with Playwright and axe.

streamingLayout.title: A chat layout that keeps the user's question in place as streamed responses grow
streamingLayout.description: I addressed the way live LLM responses push recent questions and reading context away through layout structure rather than scroll correction.

growingResponse.title: Increasing screen movement during long responses
growingResponse.description: As SSE content expanded the response block, a conventional bottom-scroll layout pushed both the user's recent question and the sentence they were reading out of view.

spacerLayout.title: A flexible spacer below the response
spacerLayout.description: I placed an empty spacer below the latest user message and in-progress AI response. Its height is the chat viewport minus the latest question and response heights, so it shrinks by the same amount whenever the response gains a line.

measurement.title: Measuring size without rendering on every change
measurement.description: ResizeObserver watches the chat viewport, latest question, and streamed response. requestAnimationFrame batches height updates to one render per frame when response chunks arrive.

streamLifecycle.title: Stream lifecycle tied to layout behavior
streamLifecycle.description: I modeled sending, streaming, done, and error states explicitly, then used AbortController to stop the previous stream when the user leaves or changes conversations. Spacer and final-scroll behavior follow those same states.

readingPosition.title: Reading position preserved
readingPosition.description:
When a user sends a question, its message scrolls near the top of the chat viewport. The spacer preserves that position until the response fills the viewport, then reaches zero and hands off to natural scrolling.

I checked that messages and available next actions match each state during response generation, completion, user cancellation, and errors.
